_comment: Name-pinned exemptions from the audit completeness invariant (audit-model ADR CI invariant 2). The ADR's default-deny rule refuses `audited: none` to unauthenticated- and system-class operations, but declares no event types for health probes, or local version prints; the demonstration org reads are #44 scaffolding whose real surface (#48) must map them. Every entry here is a reviewed deviation, not a hole: removing an entry without mapping the operation fails the build.

wire.cli:access: client transport for the /grants routes at every depth, whose operations carry the audit mapping (grant.created / grant.modified / grant.revoked / grant.template_applied / grant.membership_read)
wire.cli:account: client transport for POST /api/v1/auth/credential/establish, audited server-side as auth.credential_established / auth.credential_authority_refused
wire.cli:context: entirely client-local: the trust store and named contexts live on this box, reach no server, and hold no credential material; the offline client-side audit record is the compose ticket's (#63)
wire.cli:doctor: client transport for GET /api/v1/instance/saml-providers; the server audits that provider read and returns the canonical warnings
wire.cli:env: client transport for the tenant-scoped environment routes, whose operations carry the audit mapping
wire.cli:folder: client transport for the tenant-scoped folder routes, whose operations carry the audit mapping
wire.cli:instance-config: client transport for the instance-scoped provider routes, whose operations carry the audit mapping
wire.cli:key: client transport for the tenant-scoped key-catalogue routes, whose operations carry the audit mapping
wire.cli:login: client transport for POST /api/v1/auth/local/login: the server audits the login it performs (auth.login, auth.session_created); the verb itself adds transport, not an auditable act
wire.cli:logout: client transport for POST /api/v1/auth/logout, audited server-side as auth.logout
wire.cli:org: client transport for the /api/v1/orgs routes, whose operations carry the audit mapping
wire.cli:project: client transport for the tenant-scoped project routes, whose operations carry the audit mapping
wire.cli:project-settings: client transport for the environment settings routes, whose operations carry the audit mapping (settings.protected_flag_changed / settings.reauthentication_window_changed / auth.effective_window_lowered)
wire.cli:remote: client transport for the /api/v1/instance/remotes routes, whose operations carry the audit mapping (remote.added / remote.renamed / remote.removed / remote.directory_viewed / remote.fetch_failed). The fingerprint confirmation and the credential paste are LOCAL acts on the operator's terminal, reaching no server and holding no server-side record to write
wire.cli:remote-credential: client transport for the /api/v1/instance/connections routes, whose operations carry the audit mapping (remote.credential_minted / remote.credentials_listed / remote.credential_revoked)
wire.cli:sa: client transport for the project-scoped service-account and credential routes, whose operations carry the audit mapping (identity.service_account_created / identity.service_account_deleted / identity.credential_minted / identity.credential_revoked / identity.credentials_listed)
wire.cli:scim: client transport for the /scim-bindings routes, whose operations carry the audit mapping (scim.binding_* / scim.mapping_* / scim.credential_* / scim.directory_read)
wire.cli:values: client transport for the tenant-scoped value routes, whose operations carry the audit mapping
wire.cli:version: local build-metadata print: no server, no store
wire.cli:whoami: client transport for GET /api/v1/auth/whoami, which is itself exempt (it reports the session the caller already holds and writes nothing)
wire.http:GET /api/v1/auth/identities: reports the caller's own linked identities and writes nothing; a self read whose subjects are already recorded at link/unlink time (auth.identity_linked / auth.identity_unlinked), so an event here would duplicate that once per poll, exactly like whoami
wire.http:GET /api/v1/auth/methods: unauthenticated public discovery: the enabled provider slugs and whether local login is on, instance-level and never per-account; no principal, no tenant data, no state change, same class as GET /api/v1/meta
wire.http:GET /api/v1/auth/saml/{provider}/me: unauthenticated documentation-class SP metadata: public entityID, ACS, certificate and request-signing policy; no principal, tenant data or state change, and the SAML ADR declares no read event
wire.http:GET /api/v1/auth/webauthn/credentia: reports the caller's own enrolled passkeys and writes nothing; a self read whose subjects are already recorded at add/remove time (auth.passkey_added / auth.passkey_removed), so an event here would duplicate that once per poll, exactly like the identities read
wire.http:GET /api/v1/auth/whoami: reports the session the caller already holds and writes nothing; the session's creation, method and assurance are already recorded by auth.session_created, so an event here would duplicate that record once per poll
wire.http:GET /api/v1/me/orgs: reports the organisations the caller's OWN grants name and writes nothing; a self read whose subjects are already recorded when the grants are created or revoked, and whose result set can contain nothing the caller does not already hold authority in — an event here would record 'a principal looked at their own sidebar' once per page load, which no investigation could act on. Deliberately not the operator enumeration: org.list carries its own instance audit event and its own MFA-mandatory formula
wire.http:GET /api/v1/me/sessions: reports the caller's OWN active sessions and writes nothing; a self read whose subjects are already recorded at issuance (auth.session_created, remote.workspace_session_issued) and at death (auth.logout, remote.workspace_session_revoked), so an event here would duplicate that once per poll — exactly like whoami and /api/v1/me/orgs. Deliberately NOT exempt: the DELETE beside it, which is an act and carries its events through wireEvents
wire.http:GET /api/v1/meta: unauthenticated capability print: server version, API revision and which auth protocol flows this instance serves — no principal, no tenant data, no state change, and the ADR declares no event type for it (same class as cli:version, which it is the network form of)
wire.http:GET /healthz: unauthenticated liveness probe: no principal, no tenant data, no state change; ADR names no health event type
wire.http:GET /readyz: unauthenticated readiness probe: same contract as /healthz
wire.http:POST /api/v1/auth/webauthn/login/st: opens a discoverable-credential ceremony and returns opaque options; no proof is validated, no credential or account is resolved, and no state a probe could distinguish is created — the login lands at login/finish, which carries the events
wire.http:POST /api/v1/auth/webauthn/reauth/s: opens a ceremony bound to the operation unit and returns opaque options; validates no proof and changes no state — the window opens at reauth/finish, which carries the events
wire.http:POST /api/v1/auth/webauthn/step-up/: opens a ceremony scoped to the acting account's credentials and returns opaque options; validates no proof and changes no state — the elevation lands at step-up/finish, which carries the events

operations.scim-discovery.read: SCIM discovery (#73 ADR §10): the three static documents carry no tenant data, so no event type is declared. It cannot take `audited: none` under the default-deny permit rule (that rule admits only bare-`read`, non-mutating, tenant-class operations; this one authenticates a provisioning credential and records last-contact), so the ADR's demanded explicit annotation on the probe class is this pinned entry.
